Native themes for gratia plots

Source: R/plot-theme.R
gratia_theme_get.Rd

Gratia plots use ordinary ggplot2 themes. Component settings are read when the plot is built, so they can also be changed after calling draw().

Usage

gratia_theme_get()

gratia_theme_set(theme = NULL)

gratia_theme_update(...)

Arguments

theme

A ggplot2 theme, or NULL to clear the package override.

...

Settings passed to ggplot2::theme().

Value

gratia_theme_get() returns a theme or NULL. The setter and updater invisibly return the previous override.

Details

gratia_theme_get() returns the override stored in options("gratia.plot.theme"). It does not include ggplot2's active theme. The override is attached to each plot when it is constructed. Later changes to this option affect new plots. Use withr::with_options() for a temporary override. Unspecified settings inherit ggplot2's active theme as usual.

Component elements accept ggplot2::element_geom(). The main elements are geom.gratia.smooth, geom.gratia.effect, geom.gratia.derivative, geom.gratia.sample, geom.gratia.interval, geom.gratia.partial.residual, geom.gratia.increase, geom.gratia.decrease, geom.gratia.change, geom.gratia.diagnostic.point, geom.gratia.reference, geom.gratia.rug, geom.gratia.contour, geom.gratia.boundary, geom.gratia.observed, geom.gratia.replicated, geom.gratia.chain, geom.gratia.histogram, geom.gratia.rootogram.bar, geom.gratia.rootogram.fitted, and geom.gratia.concurvity.bar. Other elements are geom.gratia.curve (the parent of smooth, effect, derivative, sample and basis), geom.gratia.basis, geom.gratia.surface, geom.gratia.diagnostic.boxplot, geom.gratia.residual.covariate.point, geom.gratia.diagnostic.reference, geom.gratia.chain.reference, geom.gratia.correlation.reference, geom.gratia.histogram.outline, geom.gratia.rootogram.reference, geom.gratia.rootogram.warning, geom.gratia.correlation, and geom.gratia.trend.

Opacity is set separately, using numeric elements between zero and one: gratia.alpha.interval, gratia.alpha.partial.residual, gratia.alpha.diagnostic.point, gratia.alpha.rug, gratia.alpha.sample, gratia.alpha.observed, gratia.alpha.replicated, gratia.alpha.chain, gratia.alpha.histogram, and gratia.alpha.surface.interval. More specific elements, such as geom.gratia.smooth.interval, geom.gratia.diagnostic.interval, geom.gratia.surface.interval, geom.gratia.surface.rug, and their gratia.alpha.* counterparts, override the general component setting.

Standard fields such as colour, fill, linewidth, pointsize and pointshape set component defaults. Fields such as ink and borderwidth follow the parent ggplot2 geom's interpretation.

Default component settings preserve the existing plot appearance. Mapped aesthetics retain their scales. Explicit aesthetic arguments to plotting functions are deprecated but remain fixed overrides; use themes instead. Palette settings use palette.colour.discrete, palette.fill.discrete, palette.colour.continuous, and palette.fill.continuous. Complete scale objects can still be supplied through the existing scale arguments.

For a single ggplot, add a theme with +. For a patchwork returned by draw() or appraise(), use & to affect every panel. Plots delegated to bayesplot retain that package's styling.

Examples

library("ggplot2")
old <- gratia_theme_set(theme(
  geom.gratia.smooth = element_geom(colour = "navy"),
  gratia.alpha.interval = 0.15
))
gratia_theme_update(geom.gratia.contour = element_geom(colour = "grey40"))
gratia_theme_set(old)

pal <- gratia_palette("tol_banded_16")
theme(palette.colour.discrete = pal, palette.fill.discrete = pal)
#> <theme> List of 2
#>  $ palette.colour.discrete:function (n)  
#>  $ palette.fill.discrete  :function (n)  
#>  @ complete: logi FALSE
#>  @ validate: logi TRUE
